NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Unmarried villagers are not allowed to speak at the naming feasts: challenge the custom, or quietly ignore it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: By old custom, only married villagers may speak blessings at a child's naming feast. (subject) is unmarried, and is the baby's favorite aunt or uncle, and wants to speak. (friend), the baby's parent, would love that, but is worried about the elders. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) asks the elders to change the rule. There is a long and heated discussion. In the end, the elders agree that anyone who loves the child may bless it. (subject) gives the blessing, and stumbles over the words, and nobody cares.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: At the feast, after the official blessings, (friend) hands the baby to (subject), who whispers a blessing of (subject.his/her) own. A few elders notice. One of them nods. The rule is still the rule. It is a little less of one.
